_doc: CODEC FIELD SURVIVAL -- the shared matrix that says, per codec and per field,
whether an attribute-SATURATED element survives a round trip.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every codec gate in this repository (SVG parse, SVG
round-trip, canonical test-JSON round-trip, binary round-trip) compares
`document_to_test_json` STRINGS before and after. That catches a dropped field
perfectly -- but only for fields the canonical test-JSON itself emits, so the
test_json column below is not one column among three: it is the CEILING on
what any string-oracle gate in this repository can see at all.
HISTORY, because the ceiling moved and the reasoning is what justifies the
repair. Until 2026-07-28 twelve of the thirteen rows below read DROPPED for
test_json, and the set of fields the BINARY codec dropped was a strict SUBSET
of that set -- so no fixture, however saturated, could red-light a single one
of the binary codec's drops through the existing gates, and the corpus
census's prescription (5.4: 'one maximal fixture per element type') was NOT
EXECUTABLE against the string oracle. Worse, THE PRESERVATION LAW's primary
gate (transcripts/EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md 4.1) snapshots this same codec, so
an edit that destroyed a BYSTANDER's mask, blend mode, dash pattern, stroke
brush, width profile or either gradient was invisible to the law BY
CONSTRUCTION. All twelve are now carried, writer and reader, in both ports;
the ceiling is the whole matrix and the remaining DROPPED cells are real
codec gaps rather than artefacts of the oracle.
SINCE 2026-07-27 this family has a companion that watches a different
thing: test_fixtures/expected/binary_wire.json pins the binary codec's
per-tag ARITY and its exact BYTES for both ports against ONE shared
golden. This family answers 'did the field survive in this port'; that one
answers 'do the two ports write the same bytes'. Neither subsumes the
other -- a field could survive in both ports at DIFFERENT slots, and two
ports could agree byte-for-byte on dropping something.
This family sidesteps the string oracle. Both ports build the same saturated
Path IN CODE (the shape is spelled out in `saturated_path` below, and mirrored
in jas_dioxus/src/cross_language_test.rs and JasSwift/Tests/CrossLanguageTests
.swift), round-trip it, and compare field values at the MODEL level (Rust
PartialEq / Swift Equatable). The matrix below is then asserted cell by cell.
HOW TO READ A CELL. PRESERVED = the field came back equal. DROPPED = it did
not. A DROPPED cell is a PINNED gap, not an accepted one: fixing the site turns
this gate RED until the cell is updated, so a gap here can never rot into a
silent suppression (the same discipline as `expected_violations` in
test_fixtures/preservation/).
THE PRESERVATION LAW (transcripts/EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md, ratified
2026-07-27) frames every DROPPED cell: a round trip speaks to NOTHING, so it
must preserve EVERYTHING. `classification` therefore separates the two shapes
the law distinguishes, and the distinction is evidence-based, not editorial:
REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED -- the output representation demonstrably carries
this class of value ALREADY, somewhere this codebase can be pointed at (an
attribute one port writes, an attribute this port's own reader parses, or a
slot the format has been extended with before). Dropping it is a defect.
NO_COUNTERPART -- the output representation has no construct for the value
and neither port writes an extension for it. An honest representation
limit, which the law says must be DOCUMENTED rather than guessed at.
`classification` is prose analysis and is NOT machine-asserted; only
`survival` and `port_overrides` are.

saturated_path._doc: The element both ports construct in code. Recorded here so the two mirrors can be diffed against one statement of intent; it is NOT parsed by either gate (the canonical test-JSON cannot express most of these keys -- that is the whole point).
saturated_path.fill_gradient: radial, angle 45, aspect 200, smooth, dither, along-stroke, 2 stops
saturated_path.stroke_gradient: radial, angle 45, aspect 200, smooth, dither, along-stroke, 2 stops

port_overrides._doc: A cell where the two ports MEASURABLY DISAGREE today. The `survival` value above is what both ports must reach; a port listed here is asserted to produce the stated OTHER value, so closing the divergence turns this gate red until the entry is deleted. Empty is the goal state.

test_json._all_preserved: CLOSED 2026-07-28. The canonical test-JSON is a hand-built object writer that already emitted nested objects (`transform`, `fill`, `stroke`, `tspans`) and already emitted keys CONDITIONALLY on non-default (`id`, and `fill_rule` -- written only when `evenodd`). Nothing about the format ever prevented any of these keys; the writer simply had none and the reader hard-coded them away (jas_dioxus/src/geometry/test_json.rs `parse_stroke` built every Stroke with miter_limit 10.0 / align Center / an all-zero dash array, and `parse_common` wrote mask: None and mode: default). WHAT LANDED: `extended_element_fields` / `extendedElementFields` in the two ports' test_json writers, emitting all twelve conditionally on non-default so an element carrying none of them serializes byte-identically to before, plus the matching reader pass. GOLDEN CHURN, stated: 12 shipped goldens moved, and every one of them gained a key that had always been in the model and never in the JSON -- 7 blob gesture goldens gained `tool_origin`, 4 set_attr_on_selection goldens gained `stroke_brush` / `stroke_brush_overrides`, and this file is the twelfth. Nothing else in either corpus moved, which is the conditional-emission convention doing its job.
test_json.fill_rule: PRESERVED -- written at jas_dioxus/src/geometry/test_json.rs `o.str_val("fill_rule", "evenodd")` and mirrored in JasSwift/Sources/Geometry/TestJson.swift. It is the proof that the conditional-key mechanism works and generalises.
test_json._gradient_stop_colour: A CROSS-PORT MODEL DIVERGENCE the wire form does NOT resolve, recorded so it cannot be mistaken for a codec bug. jas_dioxus's GradientStop.color is a `Color` (f64 channels, rgb/hsb/cmyk, with alpha); JasSwift's is a hex `String`. The canonical test-JSON writes the stop colour as this file's shared colour OBJECT, which is lossless for every value EITHER port can hold -- but a shared fixture can still only carry a stop colour JasSwift can express, because JasSwift's reader converts the object back to hex. The BINARY codec's two gradient rows are blocked on the same fork and remain banked; see `classification.binary.fill_gradient`.
test_json._arrowheads_are_not_watched: A GAP THIS FAMILY DOES NOT WATCH, named so it is not mistaken for coverage. `stroke.start_arrow`, `stroke.end_arrow`, `stroke.start_arrow_scale`, `stroke.end_arrow_scale` and `stroke.arrow_align` are absent from the `fields` list above, so no cell measures them in ANY codec. The canonical test-JSON still drops all five; the binary codec carries them (pack_stroke is complete); the SVG codec was not measured. They are the same shape of blindness this wave closed for align / dash_pattern / dash_align_anchors / miter_limit. UNBLOCK: add the five rows here, let the gate measure all three codecs, and close whichever then read DROPPED.

binary._all_dropped: SUPERSEDED for five of the seven, 2026-07-27. History, because the reasoning is what justified the repair: the binary codec is msgpack over per-tag positional arrays and had been EXTENDED TWICE by appending slots (the `symbols` master store at document index 3, tolerated via `arr.get(3)`; the live-element instance transform at TAG_LIVE slot 9), so the seven fields were omitted, not unrepresentable -- `pack_common` carried 6 of CommonProps' 9 fields and `mode`, `mask` and `tool_origin` were hard-coded to defaults on the unpack side. Live consequence: apply a brush or set a blend mode, relaunch, and the setting was gone. WHAT LANDED: a per-tag TRAILING EXTENSION (RULED 2026-07-27, transcripts/EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md) carrying mode / mask / tool_origin on every tag and stroke_brush / stroke_brush_overrides on TAG_PATH, with `VERSION` still 2 and tolerant reads. The two gradients are NOT closed -- see `fill_gradient` below.
binary.common.mask: PRESERVED as of the 2026-07-27 extension. The mask rides its tag's extension block as [subtree, clip, invert, disabled, linked, unlink_transform], where the subtree is a FULL nested element, so the mask artwork keeps all of its own fields too.
binary.common.mode: PRESERVED as of the 2026-07-27 extension: an integer tag 0..15 in BlendMode's declaration order, mirrored in both ports, unknown tag reads as Normal.
binary.common.tool_origin: PRESERVED as of the 2026-07-27 extension, with a MODEL asymmetry that is not a codec defect: Rust carries `tool_origin` on every element's CommonProps, JasSwift only on `Path`. Both ports write the slot for every tag; JasSwift writes nil for the eleven tags whose struct has no field, exactly as it already writes nil for `name` on the live variants. A value a port cannot hold is a value it cannot lose.
binary.stroke_brush: PRESERVED as of the 2026-07-27 extension -- a TAG_PATH-only slot immediately after the common extension block.
binary.stroke_brush_overrides: PRESERVED as of the 2026-07-27 extension -- the slot after stroke_brush.
binary.fill_gradient: STILL DROPPED, and BANKED rather than guessed. The wire mechanism is not the obstacle; the two ports' gradient MODELS are. jas_dioxus's GradientStop.color is a `Color` (f64 channels, rgb/hsb/cmyk, with alpha); JasSwift's is a hex `String`. test_fixtures/algorithms/gradient_remap.json already records that divergence and rules 8-bit hex the widest value the two models SHARE. Measured consequence for a wire encoding, this wave: encoding the stop colour as the codec's existing 6-slot colour array is lossless in Rust but NORMALISES the Swift string (this fixture's own saturated stop is "#ff0000" and would come back "ff0000", so the cell would read PRESERVED in Rust and DROPPED in Swift); encoding it as a hex string is lossless in Swift but DISCARDS a Rust hsb/cmyk stop colour and its alpha. Byte-identity across the ports therefore requires a canonical form, and choosing which port normalises is an artwork-semantics call with a real cost either way. Under the adjudication hierarchy that is a ruling, not an implementation detail, so it is banked. Nothing else blocks it: the slots would append after tool_origin (and after stroke_brush_overrides on TAG_PATH).
binary.stroke_gradient: STILL DROPPED -- same fork as fill_gradient, banked with it.
binary.stroke.dash_align_anchors: PRESERVED -- pack_stroke carries the full Stroke including dash pattern, dash length, align, miter limit and both arrowheads. The census row that grouped `dash_align_anchors` and `width_points` with the binary codec's losses is corrected here by measurement: they survive.
binary._stroke_all: stroke.align, stroke.dash_pattern and stroke.miter_limit are PRESERVED for the same reason: pack_stroke is complete. The binary codec is the ONLY one of the three that carries the whole Stroke.
binary.width_points: PRESERVED -- packed for Line and Path.

svg.common.tool_origin: REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED (Rust, until this wave). `jas:tool-origin` is written by JasSwift's <path> arm AND parsed by Rust's own `parse_common` for every element -- so the representation exists, this port's reader consumes it, and only this port's writer omitted it. Closed in the same wave as this fixture.
svg.common.mask: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. SVG has <mask>, but neither port writes or reads any mask construct, and jas's Mask carries `invert`, `disabled`, `linked` and `unlink_transform` with no SVG analogue. Documented, not guessed.
svg.common.mode: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. CSS `mix-blend-mode` covers the 16 modes, but neither port writes or reads it.
svg.fill_gradient: NO_EXACT_COUNTERPART. SVG <linearGradient>/<radialGradient> exist, but jas's Gradient carries `midpoint_to_next` per stop plus `aspect_ratio`, `dither` and `stroke_sub_mode`, none of which SVG expresses. A faithful export needs a jas: extension alongside the standard element -- a design question, not a one-line fix.
svg.stroke_gradient: NO_EXACT_COUNTERPART -- as fill_gradient, plus the stroke sub-mode has no SVG meaning at all.
svg.stroke_brush: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. A jas-private reference ("<library>/<brush>"); it would ride a jas: attribute exactly as tool-origin does, but no port writes one.
svg.stroke_brush_overrides: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand -- same shape as stroke_brush.
svg.width_points: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. The variable-width profile has no SVG stroke analogue; a faithful export means emitting the OUTLINE, which is a different document, or a jas: extension.
svg.fill_rule: PRESERVED -- both ports write `fill-rule="evenodd"` and both read it.
svg.stroke.dash_align_anchors: PRESERVED -- both ports write `data-jas-dash-align-anchors="true"` and both read it.
svg.stroke.dash_pattern: PRESERVED as of CODECSAT. It was REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED in BOTH ports: `stroke-dasharray` is a STANDARD SVG presentation attribute and neither port wrote it or read it, so a dashed stroke saved to SVG came back SOLID while the jas-private flag saying HOW to lay the dashes out was carried faithfully. NOTE ON THE FIXTURE'S OWN VALUES: SVG lengths are written in px at 4 decimal places, so a pt value whose px form is not exact at 4dp does not come back bit-equal (4pt -> 5.3333px -> 3.999975pt). The saturated pattern is 3 / 1.5 / 6 / 0.75 pt = 4 / 2 / 8 / 1 px exactly, so this cell reads DROPPED only for an OMISSION and never for a rounding. Every other SVG length in this document has the same ~1e-5 property; the string-oracle gates absorb it because canonical test-JSON rounds to 4dp.
svg.stroke.miter_limit: PRESERVED as of CODECSAT. It was REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED in BOTH ports: `stroke-miterlimit` is a STANDARD SVG presentation attribute; neither port wrote it and each reader hard-coded 10.0. Unitless, so no px conversion and no rounding question.
svg.stroke.align: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. Inside/outside stroke alignment has no attribute in SVG 1.1 (`stroke-alignment` is an unshipped SVG 2 draft), so a faithful export needs a jas: extension -- which is a naming decision, not a repair, and is banked rather than guessed.
